description:
###### What this shows:
*RPC request throughput and response timing, pathfinding cost, gRPC read traffic, and resource-manager enforcement for this node.*

###### Use it to:
*Watch client request load and cost, and confirm resource limits are protecting the node.*

panels.title: RPC Request Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How many RPC requests the server counts per second.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of the RPC request counter over 5 minutes, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*A steady line proportional to client demand; cross-checks the trace-based RPC dashboard.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; tracks client activity.*

###### Watch for:
*A sudden surge above baseline, consistent with a client flooding the RPC endpoint.*

###### Source:
[ServerHandler.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/rpc/detail/ServerHandler.cpp)

###### Function:
`ServerHandler ctor`

panels.title: RPC Response Time
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The 95th-percentile end-to-end RPC response time, including HTTP handling.*

###### How it's computed:
*95th-percentile of measured response times over 5 minutes, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; this is broader than command-only latency.*

###### Healthy range:
*A few to tens of milliseconds; workload-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*A sustained climb, indicating handler overload or slow downstream work.*

###### Source:
[ServerHandler.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/rpc/detail/ServerHandler.cpp)

###### Function:
`ServerHandler ctor`

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, exported_instance) (rate(xrpld_rpc_time_milliseconds_bucket{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name"}[5m])))

panels.title: RPC Response Size
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The 95th-percentile size of RPC response payloads in bytes.*

###### How it's computed:
*95th-percentile of response payload sizes over 5 minutes, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Smaller is cheaper; large responses cost bandwidth and memory.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; small for status queries, large for bulk data queries.*

###### Watch for:
*Growth in large responses, consistent with expensive queries or API misuse.*

###### Source:
[ServerHandler.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/rpc/detail/ServerHandler.cpp)

###### Function:
`ServerHandler ctor`

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, exported_instance) (rate(xrpld_rpc_size_milliseconds_bucket{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name"}[5m])))

panels.title: RPC Response Time Distribution
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*RPC response time at the 90th, 95th, and 99th percentiles together.*

###### How it's computed:
*Three response-time quantiles over 5 minutes, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; the gap between P90 and P99 shows the long tail.*

###### Healthy range:
*Percentiles clustered low; workload-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*A widening P99, revealing long-tail or bimodal slow requests.*

###### Source:
[ServerHandler.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/rpc/detail/ServerHandler.cpp)

###### Function:
`ServerHandler ctor`

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by (le, exported_instance) (rate(xrpld_rpc_time_milliseconds_bucket{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name"}[5m])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, exported_instance) (rate(xrpld_rpc_time_milliseconds_bucket{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name"}[5m])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, exported_instance) (rate(xrpld_rpc_time_milliseconds_bucket{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name"}[5m])))

panels.title: Pathfinding Fast Duration
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The 95th-percentile time of the fast pathfinding search.*

###### How it's computed:
*95th-percentile of fast pathfinding durations over 5 minutes, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; fast mode trades accuracy for speed.*

###### Healthy range:
*Typically a few to tens of milliseconds; workload-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*A rising trend, indicating heavy pathfinding demand or an expensive order book.*

###### Source:
[PathRequestManager.h](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/rpc/detail/PathRequestManager.h)

###### Function:
`ctor`

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, exported_instance) (rate(xrpld_pathfind_fast_milliseconds_bucket{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name"}[5m])))

panels.title: Pathfinding Full Duration
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The 95th-percentile time of the full, exhaustive pathfinding search.*

###### How it's computed:
*95th-percentile of full pathfinding durations over 5 minutes, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; full mode is much more expensive than fast mode.*

###### Healthy range:
*Tens to hundreds of milliseconds; workload-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*Sustained high durations, consistent with pathfinding-heavy clients straining the node.*

###### Source:
[PathRequestManager.h](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/rpc/detail/PathRequestManager.h)

###### Function:
`ctor`

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, exported_instance) (rate(xrpld_pathfind_full_milliseconds_bucket{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name"}[5m])))

panels.title: Resource Warnings Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How often the resource manager warns a peer or client for excessive usage, per second.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of resource-warning events over 5 minutes, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Green near zero, yellow above 0.1/sec, red above 1/sec.*

###### Healthy range:
*Near zero in normal operation.*

###### Watch for:
*A rising rate, consistent with aggressive clients that may need throttling.*

###### Source:
[Logic.h](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/include/xrpl/resource/detail/Logic.h)

###### Function:
`Logic::Stats ctor`

panels.title: Resource Drops Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How often the resource manager drops or blocks a peer or client for abuse, per second.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of resource-drop events over 5 minutes, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Green near zero, yellow above 0.01/sec, red above 0.1/sec.*

###### Healthy range:
*Zero when no abusive consumers are present.*

###### Watch for:
*Non-zero values, meaning the node is actively rejecting abusive connections.*

###### Source:
[Logic.h](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/include/xrpl/resource/detail/Logic.h)

###### Function:
`Logic::Stats ctor`

panels.title: gRPC Request Rate by Method (Spans)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How many gRPC calls of each method the node serves per second.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of gRPC calls over 5 minutes, grouped by method and node.*

###### Reading it:
*Non-zero only when reporting/Clio-style clients use the gRPC API.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; zero without gRPC traffic.*

###### Watch for:
*A single method spiking, consistent with a heavy or misbehaving gRPC consumer.*

###### Source:
[GRPCServer.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/main/GRPCServer.cpp)

###### Function:
`GRPCServerImpl::CallData::process`

targets.expr: sum by (method, exported_instance) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", method=~"$grpc_method", span_name=~"grpc\\..*"}[5m]))

panels.title: gRPC Latency P95 by Method (Spans)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The 95th-percentile latency of each gRPC method.*

###### How it's computed:
*95th-percentile of gRPC call durations over 5 minutes, grouped by method and node.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; identifies slow gRPC read paths.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; scales with ledger data volume served.*

###### Watch for:
*A method whose latency climbs, indicating an expensive read path.*

###### Source:
[GRPCServer.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/main/GRPCServer.cpp)

###### Function:
`GRPCServerImpl::CallData::process`

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, method, exported_instance) (rate(traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", method=~"$grpc_method", span_name=~"grpc\\..*"}[5m])))

panels.title: gRPC Error Rate by Status (Spans)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*gRPC call rate broken down by outcome status (success or error).*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of gRPC calls over 5 minutes, grouped by status and node.*

###### Reading it:
*Success should dominate; the error rate should stay low.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; errors near the floor.*

###### Watch for:
*A rising error rate, indicating gRPC clients hitting failures.*

###### Source:
[GRPCServer.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/main/GRPCServer.cpp)

###### Function:
`GRPCServerImpl::CallData::process`

targets.expr: sum by (grpc_status, exported_instance) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name=~"grpc\\..*", grpc_status!=""}[5m]))

panels.title: Pathfinding Compute Duration (Spans)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The 95th-percentile time to compute paths for a single request.*

###### How it's computed:
*95th-percentile of path-computation durations over 5 minutes, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; complements the fast/full pathfinding timers with span-level detail.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; grows with order-book depth and request complexity.*

###### Watch for:
*A rising trend under pathfinding load, indicating expensive path computation.*

###### Source:
[PathRequest.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/rpc/detail/PathRequest.cpp)

###### Function:
`PathRequest::doUpdate`

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, exported_instance) (rate(traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="pathfind.compute"}[5m])))

panels.title: Pathfinding Request & Discovery Rate (Spans)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The rate of client path requests versus path-discovery passes.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rates of path requests and discovery passes over 5 minutes, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Discovery cost tracks request demand; useful for subscription-heavy nodes.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; both zero without pathfinding clients.*

###### Watch for:
*Discovery rate climbing out of proportion to requests, a cost driver for subscription-heavy nodes.*

###### Source:
[PathFind.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/rpc/handlers/orderbook/PathFind.cpp) · [PathRequest.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/rpc/detail/PathRequest.cpp)

###### Function:
`doPathFind ; PathRequest::findPaths`
